newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DB Fund Management launch new Singapore dlr fund.
newsitem.headline: DB Fund Management launch new Singapore dlr fund.

text.p: DB Fund Management Ltd, a subsidiary of the Deutsche Bank Group is to launch a new Singapore dollar denominated fund on August 6, the company said on Tuesday.
It said in a statement the DB Lion Bond Fund was an open ended unit trust that will invest mainly in Single A and above quality investment grade medium-term bonds.
It will invest not just in Singapore dollar bonds but bonds in major currencies issued by governments, supranational bodies, prime corporations and financial institutions.
To give the fund a Singapore dollar profile, all foreign currency investments will be fully hedged into Sing dollars.
The minimum investment required S$5,000 with the initial offer priced at S$10.20 per unit including a two percent preliminary charge. There will be a discount for investors buying before August 5.

"This fund is targeted toward both retail and corporate investors looking for a conservative but flexible investment tool that aims to outperform short-duration fixed income instruments," DB Fund Management managing director Oliver Behrens said in the statement.

"The current volatility in the equity markets makes the DB Lion Bond Fund particularly attractive as part of an overall investment portfolio. For institutions and corportions, it should prove to be a very valuable cash management tool."
